Title: EU to ban social media for under 13s, curb access until 15
Article:
STRASBOURG, France:  The European Union will ban social media for children under 13 and allow only limited, supervised access until the age of 15 under plans unveiled Wednesday by EU chief Ursula von der Leyen.
A global backlash against social media has piled pressure on policymakers, with a rising body of evidence showing negative impacts on children's physical and mental health.
"It is time for Europe to act," von der Leyen said during her annual keynote address to the European Parliament. "It is we who decide our rules, not big tech," she warned.
Australia last year became the first country to ban social media for under-16s, triggering similar moves elsewhere, but the European Commission chief said the 27-country bloc would take a more "gradual" approach.
"No social media under the age of 13. No personal account under the age of 15," she said. "That means from 13 to under 15, only mini accounts, set up and supervised by parents or guardians, with limited features and time restriction to one hour a day."
"And between 15 and 18, safe design will be an obligation for the platforms."
Before outlining the EU's approach, von der Leyen paid tribute to a 14-year-old girl in Belgium, named Olea, who killed herself one month ago after being bullied, and whose mother she quoted as saying: "I am convinced that without these omnipresent networks, my daughter would still be here."
Von der Leyen made no reference to online games or AI chatbots, which according to draft legislation seen by AFP would also be hit by the restrictions.
The commission president and tech chief Henna Virkkunen will formally present the proposed "KIDS Act", including the tiered age limits in Strasbourg, France on Thursday.
Children's rights and parents groups welcomed moves to make online platforms safer.
"The devil is of course in the detail. Tomorrow's proposal must be coherent, comprehensive, future-proof and robustly enforceable," the 5Rights Foundation advocacy group's Leanda Barrington-Leach said.
"Finally Europe is sending a clear signal: it's time to act against the harmful design of platforms to protect our children from toxic algorithms and features," said Arnaud Ducoin, part of a group of French families who have filed a complaint against TikTok over teenagers' self-harm and suicides.
'ARBITRARY AGE THRESHOLD'
The new EU law will also ban addictive design features such as so-called infinite scrolling where children are concerned, according to a draft document.
If platforms break the rules, they face fines of up to six percent of annual turnover, draft details show.
"We do not have to accept addictive features," von der Leyen warned, saying "platforms will have to prove that they are safe."
The "risk" is not limited to children, she noted. "Addictive design, for example, is harming everyone," she said, telling EU lawmakers that Europe needed more rules that will be proposed in the autumn.
Simeon de Brouwer of digital rights group EDRi said making platforms safer across the board was an urgent necessity, telling AFP "if the design is harmful at 13, it does not magically become safe on their 15th or 18th birthday."
PRESSURE FROM EU STATES
Von der Leyen had faced pressure from members including France, Denmark and Greece for action across the 27-nation bloc to limit online harms for children.
France, which has proposed its own legislation, welcomed the announcement. Government spokeswoman Maud Bregeon said it was "a step in the right direction."
The EU has sought for years to rein in Big Tech, empowering itself with a strengthened legal armoury, but it believes additional tools are needed to limit online harms.
The bloc has already told Meta platforms Facebook and Instagram as well as TikTok to change their "addictive" design through its content law known as the Digital Services Act, but changes have taken longer than Brussels wants.
Digital and consumer rights groups have meanwhile raised concerns over a related age-check app due to be rolled out later this year which Brussels says will keep children off social media.
"Age verification is not a silver bullet and would raise serious privacy and data protection concerns," said European consumer organisation BEUC's Agustin Reyna.
Thursday's proposal will only become law after negotiations between EU capitals and the European Parliament, which could take months.

Title: Health minister visits family of FDS nurse killed in heli crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad visited the late nurse Debra Moset at their home in Rabak Rimu, Kampung Semadang, Padawan, today.
The visit was to convey his condolences in person to the family and hand over assistance to help ease their burden following Debra's death in the
Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash
in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, last week.
A social media post on the Health Ministry's Facebook page today showed Dzulkefly spending time with members of Debra's family, including her mother, Renog Rasas, 71, and the late nurse's children.
He also offered words of encouragement to Debra's children, urging them to remain committed to their studies and pursue their aspirations.
The visit was also attended by Health Ministry secretary-general Datuk Seri Hasnol Zam Zam Ahmad and Sarawak Health Department deputy director (Management) Banges Munga.
Debra, 40, was among five people killed when an FDS helicopter crashed near the Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing (STOL) port in Ulu Baram on Sept 8.
The other victims were pilot Capt Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33; assistant medical officer Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and staff nurse Jessie Paya Jok, 44.
The BO-105 helicopter, registered as 9M-LLF, crashed at about 3.21pm while attempting to land at the STOL port.
Debra, who had served with the FDS for several years, was laid to rest at the Kampung Semadang cemetery on Sept 14.
Her family had earlier described her as a cheerful person who loved cooking and regularly returned to her hometown to spend time with her family.
The remains of all five victims were subsequently handed over to their next of kin after DNA identification was completed.
The FDS in Sarawak was also temporarily
suspended
to facilitate investigations and a comprehensive safety assessment.

Title: 19 hikers rescued after four-hour ordeal at Lata Debu
Article:
BALING: Firefighters rescued 19 people who were trapped following a flash flood at Lata Debu today.
District fire and rescue station chief Zulkhairi Mat Tanjil said his team received a distress call at 4.11pm.
Zulkhairi, who led the operation with eight firefighters, said they had to trek 2km to reach the location.
"Upon arrival, we found 19 people, comprising nine women and 10 men aged between 20 and 25, who were believed to have been trapped by a flash flood.
"They were believed to have been making their way down when they became trapped following the flash flood and strong currents," he said when contacted today.
He said a river-crossing method using ropes was employed to rescue the victims one by one.
He said all the victims were rescued safely, with the operation taking almost four hours due to slippery rocks and strong river currents.
"Heavy rain that fell in the district for almost two hours today caused the flash flood.
"All 19 people began their hike at Lata Debu at 8am and became trapped by the flash flood while making their way down," he said.
He said all of them were safe and did not suffer any injuries.
He said the group was believed to be from outside the area and had come to hike there.
He said this was the second operation involving an incident at Lata Debu this month, with the first taking place last Sunday when one person fainted and two other hikers went missing.
"Lata Debu has beautiful scenery, so many people are interested in coming here.
"The operation ended at 8.10pm and all of them were handed over to the police," he said.

Title: Kosovo's ex-president Thaci jailed for 25 years for war crimes
Article:
PRISTINA: Kosovo's former president Hashim Thaci was sentenced to 25 years by a tribunal in The Hague on Wednesday for war crimes, the court said in a long-awaited verdict likely to spark outrage in the Balkan country.
The judges said Thaci, who was tried along with three other former guerrilla leaders, was guilty of illegal arrests, torture, murder and cruel treatment committed by guerrilla fighters.
In Kosovo's capital, a large crowd gathered to watch live on large screens the sentencing of a man many revere as a hero.
As the decision was delivered, the crowd fell silent, with many appearing to be shocked by the decision – after weeks of preparation by his supporters for his possible acquittal.
Thaci's fellow former Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) figures Jakup Krasniqi, Rexhep Selimi and Kadri Veseli were also found guilty and sentenced.
Krasniqi received 25 years in prison, Selimi got 13 years and Veseli 18 years.
All four were determined to be criminally responsible for the arbitrary detention and torture of hundreds of people and 96 murders, according to the court.
But they were acquitted of crimes against humanity charges.
The court also said Thaci, Veseli, Selimi and Krasniqi had "contributed significantly" during the Kosovo conflict to a common criminal purpose targeting perceived opponents of the KLA's political and military goals.Thaci resigned as president and surrendered to the court after his 2020 indictment. He has remained in detention in The Hague ever since, with his time served counted toward his sentence.
'SAD, UNJUST'
For many inside Kosovo, Thaci and the KLA are symbols of its independence movement.
After the war, Thaci remained a central political figure and was instrumental in its 2008 declaration of independence.
Throughout the trial, images of the 58-year-old, who also served as prime minister, have regularly appeared on huge billboards around the country.
"A terrible judgment for Kosovo, for our liberation war. It is a sad, unjust, undeserved decision," Kosovo Foreign Minister Glauk Konjufca told media outside the court.
Expectations of a possible release of Thaci and his co-accused drew huge crowds for a rally over the weekend and on Wednesday, hundreds gathered in the capital again ahead of the verdict as clocks ticked down to the decision.
But once it became clear the former president would remain in detention, the square was almost deserted within minutes.
COURTING CONTROVERSY
The Kosovo Specialist Chambers (KSC), although based in the Netherlands and staffed by international judges, was established under Kosovo law specifically to prosecute alleged crimes committed by KLA members during the war.
Before the court was established, earlier cases in Kosovo largely failed because of alleged witness intimidation and political interference.
Deeply unpopular from its foundation, the court's use of evidence supplied by Belgrade, which still refuses to recognise its former province's independence, has further inflamed accusations of political bias.
Prosecutors have tried throughout the trial to distinguish between the country's independence struggle and the men on trial.
They say all four men are responsible for crimes committed against prisoners held at KLA detention facilities in Kosovo and neighbouring Albania, as well as the politically motivated murders of Serb, Albanian and Roma civilians.
The crimes were committed during and just after the Kosovo war, which claimed some 13,000 lives.
In response, the men's lawyers had argued that the KLA lacked a strict command structure and the senior figures could not control or be held responsible for fighters who committed crimes.

Title: Angkasa president elected to ICA Board, Malaysia retains seat in global cooperative body
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Angkatan Koperasi Kebangsaan Malaysia Bhd (Angkasa) president Datuk Seri Dr Abdul Fattah Abdullah has been elected as an International Cooperative Alliance (ICA) Board member for the 2026-2030 term.
In a statement, Angkasa said the victory came through an election held during the ICA General Assembly 2026 in Panama, enabling Malaysia to retain its place in the top leadership of the world cooperative movement's apex body.
Angkasa vice president Datuk Kamarudin Ismail's held the same position for the 2022-2026 term.
"Fifteen Board members were elected from 24 candidates for the 2026 to 2030 term. Of that number, seven were re-elected while eight are new, including Datuk Seri Abdul Fattah Abdullah.
"A total of 116 voters representing 193 ICA member organisations from 66 countries participated in the election," the statement read.
Dr Ariel Guarco of Argentina was re-elected unopposed as ICA president. The ICA Global Board comprises 30 members: the president, four regional vice presidents, eight sectoral organisation representatives, 15 Board members and the Presidents of the Youth and Gender Equality Committees.
In the same statement, Fattah described the achievement as both an honour and a great trust, not only for Angkasa, but for the entire Malaysian cooperative movement, encompassing 16,468 cooperatives with 7.3 million members.
"This is a victory for the Malaysian cooperative movement. It proves the confidence that international cooperative leaders have in Malaysia's ability to continue contributing ideas, experience, and leadership in shaping the direction of the global cooperative movement.
"Angkasa will use this platform to ensure that the voice and interests of Malaysian cooperatives continue to be heard, while also expanding strategic networks, economic cooperation with cooperatives worldwide," he said.
Fattah is also president of the Asean Co-operative Organisation (ACO) and Vice President of the International Cooperative Alliance Asia and Pacific (ICA-AP).
He said the ICA Board position gives Angkasa a platform to shape international cooperative policy and agenda with Malaysian perspectives, especially on sustainable development, economic inclusion, inter-cooperative trade and community development.
Held as part of the ICA Global Conference & Assemblies 2026, the ICA General Assembly 2026 carries the theme 'Building Bridges: Cooperative Contribution for Peaceful World'.
It brings together leaders and international organisations to discuss how cooperatives can build peace, strengthen cooperation, and weather a shifting global economic landscape.
Fattah led a 25-member delegation to the conference. They comprised representatives from the Malaysian Cooperative Institute, Angkasa, Koperasi Pembiayaan Syariah Angkasa Bhd, Bank Kerjasama Rakyat Malaysia Bhd, Koperasi Sahabat Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia Bhd, Koperasi Angkatan Tentera Malaysia Bhd, and several other cooperatives.
Angkasa has been a full member of the ICA since May 16, 1972, and continues to play an active role in the network and leadership of the international cooperative movement.
Founded in 1895, the ICA is the apex body of the global cooperative movement, representing approximately one billion cooperative members and around three million cooperatives worldwide.

Title: Anwar, Abang Johari witness official handover of Bintulu Port to Sarawak
Article:
KUCHING: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg today witnessed the official handover of Bintulu Port to the Sarawak state government from the federal government, marking a new chapter in the management of the strategic port.
The handover was particularly significant as it took place as Sarawak hosted the national-level Malaysia Day 2026 celebrations today.
At the handover ceremony held at the Kuching International Airport, Transport Minister Anthony Loke represented the federal government, while Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas represented the state government.
According to a statement by the Sarawak Ministry of Infrastructure and Port Development, the handover involved four key documents, namely the Ports (Privatisation) (Amendment of Schedule) Order 2026 and the Bintulu Port Authority (Dissolution) (Vesting Date) Order 2026.
Also handed over were documents relating to the determination of the effective date of the Declaration of an Area in the District of Bintulu to be a Federal Port (Repeal) Act 2024 and the Bintulu Port Authority (Dissolution) Act 2024.
"With the coming into force of Act 858 and Act 859 on Sept 1, Bintulu Port officially changed its status from a federal port to a state port under the jurisdiction of the Sarawak government," the statement said.
The transition also saw the dissolution of the Bintulu Port Authority (LPB), with the port authority functions taken over by the Bintulu Port Authority (Sarawak), a state statutory body established under the Port Authorities Ordinance 1961.
The statement said that effective Sept 1, 2026, all assets, rights, interests and obligations of LPB were transferred and vested in the Sarawak government.
The takeover of Bintulu Port took about three years, beginning with Abang Johari's announcement of the takeover intention on Jan 30, 2023, before the proposal was approved by the Sarawak cabinet in February that year.
The prime minister also announced the agreement to hand over Bintulu Port when tabling Budget 2024 in parliament on Oct 13, 2023.
The federal and state governments subsequently signed a memorandum of understanding on March 22, 2024, before the legislative process was finalised with the passage of the Federal Port (Repeal) Act and Bintulu Port Authority (Dissolution) Act by the Dewan Rakyat in July 2024.
On Feb 4, the federal and Sarawak governments reached an agreement on the takeover value of LPB amounting to RM1.8 billion. A "completion agreement" was subsequently signed on June 21, 2026, followed by a cheque handover ceremony from the Sarawak government to the federal government in Bintulu.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nissan to build new hybrid SUV model for Europe at its UK plant
Article:
LONDON: Japanese automaker Nissan said on Wednesday it would build a new hybrid small SUV for Europe at its UK plant in Sunderland and would invest £170 million (US$229 million) to assemble it there.
The company said the Kicks e-POWER hybrid would be made in Sunderland alongside the Qashqai, Juke and electric Leaf models, but it did not provide a timeline for production.
Nissan has been restructuring to slash costs by ditching plants, cutting jobs and shelving some future models, including the electric version of the Qashqai.
There have been concerns over the future of the Sunderland plant, which is Britain's largest car assembly plant.
Nissan said in June it was exploring renting out one of the two production lines at Sunderland to rapidly-expanding Chinese automaker Chery to build cars there.
Reuters reported later that month that the British government was in advanced talks with Nissan about providing it financial support in return for a long-term commitment and investment in Sunderland.
"The decision to build this new model in Sunderland is a huge vote of confidence in the UK's manufacturing expertise and automotive future," Britain's business minister Jonathan Reynolds said in a statement.

Title: Volvo Malaysia rolls out electric EX30 Cross Country
Article:
VOLVO Car Malaysia has introduced the locally assembled Volvo EX30 Cross Country, an all-electric compact SUV designed for urban driving and light off-road use.
Deliveries and showroom viewings have begun nationwide.
Priced from RM218,888, excluding insurance, the model is the first fully electric vehicle in Volvo's Cross Country range.
It builds on the standard EX30 platform with increased ground clearance, all-wheel drive and styling changes intended to improve its suitability for rougher terrain.
The EX30 Cross Country is powered by a twin-motor all-wheel-drive system producing 428hp and 543Nm of torque.
It accelerates from zero to 100km/h in 3.7 seconds and offers a claimed driving range of up to 437km under the WLTP testing cycle.
Its 69kWh nickel-manganese-cobalt battery can charge from 10-80 per cent in 27 minutes using a 175kW DC rapid charger.
Compared with the standard EX30, the Cross Country has 19mm more ground clearance, and its chassis and wheel configuration are designed to improve ride comfort and stability over uneven surfaces.
The vehicle also comes with multiple sensors and radar systems supporting 360-degree environmental awareness, as well as Volvo's suite of driver-assistance and collision-avoidance technologies.
Volvo Car Malaysia and Thailand managing director Chris Wailes said the model was suited to Malaysia's combination of urban environments and access to natural landscapes.
The EX30 Cross Country features a minimalist interior using materials including upcycled denim textiles and bio-attributed Nordico upholstery.
Its infotainment system includes Google services through a 12.3-inch centre display, alongside wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto connectivity.
Cargo capacity stands at 318 litres with all seats in place, increasing to 718 litres with the rear seats folded.
Storage features include larger door compartments, a central storage area and a removable rear storage box.
The model is offered in Crystal White, Vapour Grey and Cloud Blue.
Volvo also announced updated pricing for the EX30 Ultra, which now starts from RM198,888, excluding insurance, and is available in four exterior colours.
The launch also coincides with the introduction of Volvo Car Malaysia's Digital Service Booking platform.
It allows customers to schedule aftersales appointments through the company's website or the Volvo Cars app.
The service is initially available at authorised retailers in the Klang Valley, with nationwide expansion planned.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: McLaren to invest US$675 million to expand UK manufacturing, launch SUV model
Article:
LONDON: British supercar maker McLaren said on Tuesday it would invest £500 million (US$675 million) in its UK manufacturing and engineering operations and add new models, including its first-ever SUV, to lift sales and pursue far higher profit margins to rival the likes of Ferrari.
McLaren's investments will include a new UK assembly plant, and it will develop and build its own transmissions and engines, which it said would create 1,000 direct and indirect jobs by 2032.
"McLaren Automotive is doubling down on Britain," UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said in a statement.
The firm's expansion plan comes as automakers across the industry are restructuring. Nissan is ditching plants and some future models. Jaguar Land Rover is cutting staff while Volkswagen's supervisory board has just approved a turnaround plan that includes sweeping job cuts.
McLaren CEO Nick Collins told Reuters the company's investment plan comes after restructuring last year following its acquisition by Abu Dhabi's CYVN Holdings, which also bought a non-controlling stake in McLaren's Formula One business. The automaker's main shareholder now is Abu Dhabi's sovereign wealth fund L'IMAD.
L'IMAD has committed to investing 1.5 billion pounds in McLaren over the next five years.
McLaren slashed bloated dealer stocks last year by cutting one of two production shifts at the assembly plant at its headquarters in Woking, England, and has now switched to making cars only when orders are placed to avoid discounting and boost residual values.
As part of the restructuring process, sales fell to around 2,000 cars in 2025 from just under 3,300 in 2024.
The new performance SUV model in development is part of a strategy of boosting sales by offering customers more options with a number of models planned, though Collins declined to provide product details or launch dates.
"We'll do it very much in a McLaren way," Collins said of the SUV. "It will bring something unique to the segment, which we think the customers will value."
SUVs have become a growth driver for luxury sports carmakers, broadening their customer base beyond traditional buyers of sports cars and grand tourers to tap into strong demand for high-end utility vehicles.      At Lamborghini, the Urus SUV has driven the brand's sales growth since its launch in 2018. Rival Ferrari has limited production of its roughly €450,000 (US$519,000) Purosangue SUV to maintain the vehicle's exclusivity.
The Bentayga SUV is luxury British automaker Bentley's top-selling model.
McLaren Chief Operating Officer Michael Straughan said the automaker needed growth to lower its material costs and lift its profits, and the way to get there was through expanding its product portfolio starting with the SUV.
McLaren has been loss-making for years, but Straughan said the company's margins could match the top performers in a segment that includes Ferrari, which has the highest profit margins in the auto industry.
"We can equal the best, but we've got a long way to go," he said.
While Ferrari has launched a fully electric model, the Luce, which received a cool response from investors and critics, McLaren CEO Collins said the automaker had no plans for an electric vehicle for now because there was no customer demand for one.
"We will do an electric vehicle when our customers ask us for one," he said. "And they're not asking."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Missing Klang angler found dead in Perak waters
Article:
SHAH ALAM: The body of an angler reported missing since Sunday was found floating in the waters off Hutan Melintang, Perak.
North Klang district police chief Assistant Commissioner Ramsay Embol said the search and rescue (SAR) team  was alerted to the discovery by a group of fishermen at 8.30am.
"The body was taken by the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) to Hutan Melintang Jetty.
"Identification by the next-of-kin confirmed that the body was that of Mohd Sharil Abd Rahman, 43-years-old.
"The body will be sent to Shah Alam Hospital for a post-mortem," he said in a statement.
Ramsay said the SAR operation to locate the two remaining victims was being conducted by the police, Maritime Malaysia, the Fire and Rescue Department, the Civil Defence Force and several other agencies.
"Any further developments will be announced from time to time," he said.
Four of the seven anglers reported missing were found safe in the waters off Sekinchan yesterday.
The victims were Mohd Shairazi Abdul Aziz, 43; Muhd Hamiszar Punirain, 45; Mohd Rizal Mohamad Sadali, 45; and Zulfikalnain Awang, 47.
Police received a report on Monday about seven local men who left to go fishing from Sementa Jetty, Sungai Kapar, Klang, on Sunday and failed to return as scheduled.

Title: 'Why didn't you come and see me?' - Dr Akmal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The plight of a family living in poor conditions without water and electricity in Merlimau has caught the attention of assemblyman Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh.
In a video uploaded by the Umno Youth chief on his social media account, the family, which has three young children, had been without electricity for two weeks and without a water supply for a long period because they had been unable to pay their bills.
Unable to pay an electricity bill amounting to RM2,387.32 and a water bill of RM5,000, the family had resorted to using candles at night, while relying on neighbours for water.
In the video, Dr Akmal was seen expressing shock at the condition of the house occupied by the family, which was partially without a roof.
He was also seen reprimanding a man who was the head of the family for not meeting him and informing him of the problems they were facing.
"Why didn't you come and see me? I'm embarrassed. I only found out about this from someone else. If you were living alone, I wouldn't mind. But you have young children, including a two-month-old baby.
"I feel terrible knowing someone is living in darkness like this, with children, including a two-month-old. But you have to promise me that you won't stop working.
"If I find out that you're not working, I'll look for you tomorrow," he said in the video.
Dr Akmal also expressed sadness over the family's living conditions and wanted their house to be repaired.
"I feel guilty. There are lights elsewhere, but it turns out there is someone in my area without electricity. Your house has electricity, but this family has none.
"You have water, but this family has no water. One day, that is why I cannot enter heaven," he said.
Dr Akmal was also seen paying the family's outstanding electricity bill and resolving their water supply issue, while reminding the man that the payment was not made using allocation funds but from his own salary.
"What I'm paying for is not from an allocation. This is from my own salary. So, since it is my salary, I consider it a debt you owe me.
"The way you repay this debt is by taking care of your children and not stopping work. This is the amount you owe, RM2,387.32," he said while advising the head of the family.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Five Orang Asli held at Tasek Bera released on police bail
Article:
BERA: The five Orang Asli arrested for allegedly obstructing an enforcement team during a joint operation at the Tasek Bera Conservation Forest Reserve (Ramsar) yesterday have been released on police bail.
District police chief Superintendent Zulkiflee Nazir said the five, including four women aged between 30 and 65, were released about 5pm today.
"They were released on police bail after their statements were recorded.
"The five were detained after they provoked enforcement personnel and refused to comply with our instructions," he said when contacted today.
They were investigated under Section 186 of the Penal Code for voluntarily obstructing a civil servant in the discharge of public functions.
The offence carries a maximum jail term of two years, a fine of up to RM10,000, or both, upon conviction.
It was reported that the Orang Asli from Kampung Pathir had set up barriers and allegedly
provoked enforcement
personnel who were conducting an operation under the National Forestry Act 1984 about 10am yesterday.
The enforcement operation involved the Pahang State Enforcement Unit, Forestry Department, Bera District and Land Office, General Operations Force, Wildlife and National Parks Department and police.
The special operation, which began on Sept 14, was aimed at curbing land encroachment at the Tasek Bera forest reserve.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pas chief Hadi gives statement over US claim to topple BN govt
Article:
KOTA BARU: Police have recorded a statement from Pas president Tan Sri Abdul Hadi Awang over his claim that the United States (US) offered cooperation to topple the Barisan Nasional (BN) government in 2014.
Pas president's political secretary Mohd Syahir Che Sulaiman said Hadi gave the statement in Kuala Lumpur several days ago.
"Tan Sri Tuan Guru (Hadi) has given a statement to the police several days ago in Kuala Lumpur.
"We understand that the matter is still under investigation and several witnesses have also been called.
"Further,
Tuan Guru leaves the matter to the police
and does not want to comment further out of respect for the investigation process," he said when contacted today.
Media previously reported that Hadi, in his winding-up speech at the 72nd PAS annual muktamar on Sept 5, claimed several Pas leaders were invited to a meeting at the US Embassy during then-president Barack Obama's visit to Malaysia in 2014.
He claimed the foreign parties had offered assistance to topple the government at the time.
The US Embassy, however, denied Hadi's claim.
David H Gamble Jr, who heads the US Embassy in Kuala Lumpur, said the United States had never sought to determine Malaysia's political leadership.
Following this, police began an investigation under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 after receiving 12 police reports.
Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar said 12 police reports had been lodged over the matter.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Armed forces proved capabilities in NATO mission, says veteran
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The professionalism and capabilities of the armed forces came to the fore on the world stage when it made history as the first military force from Asia to participate in a North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) mission through the Implementation Force (IFOR), a peace enforcement force, in Bosnia in 1995.
Armed forces veteran Major General (Rtd) Datuk Mohamad Raih Ismail said that before being accepted to participate in the more challenging IFOR mission, the Malaysian contingent first underwent rigorous tests by NATO.
He said that during the transition from the peacekeeping force to IFOR, the MAF successfully relocated 1,533 personnel, along with hundreds of vehicles, including Condor armoured vehicles, in heavy snowfall and sub-zero temperatures.
"The movement, which took a month, was completed without a single accident," he said this while sharing his experience under the topic 'Veteran ATM: Mewarisi Kehebatan, Memperkasa Masa Hadapan' during the Apa Khabar Malaysia programme produced by Bernama TV today.
He said the achievement also attracted the attention of the British military, which was impressed as its own forces had recorded accidents and fatalities while facing extreme weather conditions.
Raih also shared his experience of the country contingent's participation in Operation United Shield in Somalia in 1995, which saw Task Force Malaysia deployed with two ships, KD Mahawangsa and KD Inderasakti, to protect the withdrawal mission of United Nations (UN) peacekeepers under UNOSOM II.
He said the operation was carried out alongside military forces from seven countries, including the United States, Italy and France, and was successfully completed on March 2, 1995, without any problems.
"The best experience we gained was proving that our forces could work with other foreign military forces at a very professional level," he said.
Raih joined the armed forces in 1970 after being commissioned into the Royal Malay Regiment, and served in various roles as staff and commander at company, battalion, brigade and division levels.
He also served as assistant defence attaché in the Philippines during the People Power Revolution.

Title: Malaysia, Indonesia agree to cooperate on transboundary haze
Article:
KUCHING: Malaysia and Indonesia have agreed to cooperate in tackling transboundary haze, which has affected air quality in several countries in the region.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he discussed the issue with Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto while in New Delhi, India, recently.
"Yes, it was raised. We will cooperate to reduce the impact of transboundary haze," he told reporters after the official handover of Bintulu Port from the Federal Government to the Sarawak Government at Kuching International Airport here today.
Anwar was responding to questions about his meeting with Prabowo on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit in New Delhi.
He declined to elaborate, saying he was rushing to the Borneo Kuching Convention Centre (BCCK) to attend Malaysia Day celebrations.
[[nid:1534188]]
Meanwhile, the takeover of Bintulu Port by the Sarawak Government followed negotiations between the two governments before the deal was finalised in June.
On June 21, Sarawak completed a RM1.8 billion payment to the Federal Government for the transfer of ownership, assets and responsibilities related to the port.
The Sarawak Government officially took over the management and administration of Bintulu Port on Sept 1, following the repeal of the Bintulu Port Authority Act, which came into effect on Aug 31.
The official handover today was carried out by Transport Minister Anthony Loke to Sarawak Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Douglas Uggah Embas, witnessed by Anwar and Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Abang Openg.
The transfer of Bintulu Port from a federal to a state port is seen as a significant development in the implementation of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63), as well as reflecting cooperation and understanding between the Federal Government and Sarawak.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Senior citizen suffers burns after motorcycle catches fire in Jelutong
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A 72-year-old man suffered first-degree burns to his hands and legs after his motorcycle caught fire in Jelutong.
The Fire and Rescue Department said it received an emergency call at 2.05pm involving a Honda EX5 at Jalan Lenggong, Symphony Park.
Firefighters from the Jalan Perak fire and rescue station brought the blaze under control at 2.15pm.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director John Sagun Francis said the motorcycle was estimated to have been 60 per cent damaged in the fire.
"The victim was given initial treatment by Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) personnel before being taken to Penang Hospital for further examination," he said.
Photos of the badly burnt motorcycle have since gone viral.
The case has been handed over to the Fire Investigation Team (FIO).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] 'Please have mercy': Tasek Bera Orang Asli seek talks over eviction
Article:
BERA: Orang Asli villagers living near Tasek Bera are seeking negotiations with the authorities after receiving notices in June ordering them to vacate parts of the forest reserve, saying the land has been their source of livelihood for generations.
The Semelai community questioned the timing of the move, saying their families had depended on the land for more than five decades, earning a living from rubber and oil palm plantations.
Now facing eviction, they want a dialogue with the authorities, hoping their long-standing ties to the customary land (tanah adat) will be taken into consideration.
Enforcement team members attempted to enter several villages and smallholdings, including Kampung Pathir, on Sept 14 but were stopped by villagers who had erected barriers.
The tense situation at Kampung Pathir, about 10am, led to the arrest of five people, including four women.
Kampung Pathir Tok Batin Amir Noor Tan, 49, said several Orang Asli villages around Tasek Bera received pink warning notices from the Forestry Department in June for allegedly encroaching into the permanent forest reserve.
"We lodged a police report before setting up guard posts at all the village entrances and smallholdings around Tasek Bera... we have people stationed at the posts around the clock.
"We met Pahang Orang Asli Affairs Committee chairman Datuk Seri Syed Ibrahim Syed Ahmad in Temerloh to seek the withdrawal of the notices, while all the village headmen jointly sent a letter to the Menteri Besar's office asking it to look into the matter, but no action was taken," he said when met at the settlement today.
Amir Noor said several enforcement agencies led by the Pahang State Enforcement Unit arrived on Sept 14 and conducted drone surveillance of the area.
"They did not seek our permission or mention that they would be measuring our land.
"The situation became tense when the enforcement team tried to enter the village. Some refused to give in, which led to the arrest of five villagers here," he said.
Amir Noor said the enforcement team had yet to return to Kampung Pathir, adding that he was informed they had gone to other settlements near the lake today.
He said more than 7,000 Orang Asli lived in 11 settlements surrounding the lake, which he described as the main settlement area for the Semelai tribe in Pahang.
"All the villagers are connected to Tasik Bera, Sungai Bera and Sungai Serting. What are we going to do if our smallholdings within the forest reserve are taken away?" he said.
He added that Kampung Pathir had not received the notice, although enforcement team members had already entered the settlement.
Amir Noor expressed frustration over the incident, saying the Tok Batin used to be the first person consulted before authorities entered a village.
[[nid:1534207]]
"These days, it is as though we (Tok Batin) no longer exist and our roles are being sidelined," he said, claiming none of the villages near the lake had been gazetted as Orang Asli villages.
He also dismissed claims on social media that the Orang Asli community in Tasek Bera had been instigated by outsiders to rebel against the authorities.
"We do not need third parties to advise us on the matter, as our families have lived here for a long time, even before Tasek Bera was gazetted as a Ramsar site," he said, adding that they previously planted padi near the lake.
The New Straits Times visited several settlements near Tasek Bera today. Most had guard posts, although many villagers appeared reluctant to speak.
Meanwhile, mother-of-three Zaitun Gosi, 60, said the villagers would have no land to work on if the forest reserve land was taken over by the state authorities.
"Please have some mercy on us. We have been staying here for a long time. Why are we only now being told to vacate our land in the forest reserve?" she said.
Villager Lama Kaya, 60, said the development was disturbing for the Orang Asli community living by the lake, as their future was now uncertain.
"The authorities should speak to us and explain what they are planning to do with our land," he said.
A copy of the Forestry Department notice dated June 25, 2026, sighted by the NST stated that the offence was committed under Section 81(g) of the National Forestry Act 1985 for allegedly trespassing into a permanent forest reserve without authorisation.
The notice ordered the occupants to vacate the area within 14 days.
NST has reached out to Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail's office, Syed Ibrahim and Pahang Orang Asli Development Department (Jakoa) director Adam Zaidi Mahidin for their responses to the enforcement operation.
Meanwhile, Kemayan assemblyman Khaizulnizam Mohd Zuldin told the New Straits Times that Pahang Orang Asli Affairs Committee chairman Datuk Seri Syed Ibrahim Syed Ahmad had recently visited villages around Tasek Bera.
"As far as I am concerned, the Orang Asli community near Tasek Bera can continue to occupy their homes. The Pahang government is prepared to listen to and study their needs.
"I believe there is still room for discussions on the matter, as we do not want the issue to be politicised. We must be careful when dealing with land matters as they are sensitive," he said when contacted.
Khaizulnizam said the Pahang government would uphold the decree of the Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, that the Orang Asli community must not be misled into believing that every area they claim as "customary land" (tanah adat) automatically belongs to them.
[[nid:1534206]]
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze: Selangor to review follow-up measures on Friday
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Selangor government will review follow-up measures to address the deteriorating haze situation, said Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
He said the matter would be discussed in detail, based on reports from all relevant parties, at the Selangor state executive council meeting scheduled for Friday.
"This Friday we have an exco meeting. We will carefully discuss the follow-up measures, because after it (haze) cleared a bit on Sunday, the situation worsened again, especially yesterday and today. We will see on Friday according to reports from all parties," he said.
He said this after launching the Festival Turath Islami Malaysia 2026, at Masjid Putra today, which was held in conjunction with the Festival Turath Islami Malaysia 2026.
Amirudin said the state government also needs to obtain information from the State Health Department and related agencies before determining the appropriate measures.
"Appropriate measures include trying to assist at school and supervising our children while they study. This is because they spend a considerable amount of time at school, and we need to limit outdoor activities to avoid exposure to the haze and similar conditions," said Amirudin.
Six areas in Selangor recorded Air Pollution Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels as of 4.30pm today.
According to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, six areas in Selangor recorded unhealthy levels, namely Johan Setia (183), Shah Alam (170), Petaling Jaya (164), Klang (160), and both Banting and Kuala Selangor (159).
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality; 51 to 100 (moderate); 101 to 200 (unhealthy); 201 to 300 (very unhealthy); and above 301 (hazardous).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: DOE records 1,418 enforcement, monitoring actions amid haze
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Department of Environment (DOE) carried out 1,418 enforcement and monitoring actions nationwide during the haze period from Aug 3 to Sept 13.
Its deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said the actions included 978 monitoring activities, 83 field directives, 31 instruction notices, 305 cases referred to other agencies for further action, 11 compound offers, and 10 land title searches to support investigations and court proceedings.
"These efforts reflect the DOE's ongoing commitment to detecting and preventing open burning, as well as taking action against potential sources of pollution that could worsen air quality during haze episodes," she said in a statement today.
She said enforcement efforts are also strengthened through inspections and patrols in areas identified as high-risk, including agricultural land, peatlands, plantations, landfill sites and locations prone to open burning.
She said any offences identified during inspections and investigations will be followed by further action, based on the evidence gathered in the field.
Meanwhile, Azuri Azizah said Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at 3pm today showed unhealthy air quality in 37 areas, including Johan Setia in Selangor, which recorded the highest reading at 184, followed by Cheras in Kuala Lumpur at 175, Nilai in Negri Sembilan at 172, and Putrajaya and Shah Alam, both at 171.
She said the situation occurred amid persistent dry weather in parts of the southern Asean region, adding that according to the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) report yesterday, 240 hotspots were detected in Kalimantan, 355 in Sumatra and one in Malaysia (Sabah).
She said the ASMC also reported moderate to dense transboundary haze over Kalimantan, Sumatra, Peninsular Malaysia, Singapore, and parts of southern Vietnam and Cambodia.
Meanwhile, Azuri Azizah said the DOE is paying particular attention to fires in Sarawak, especially those involving peatlands and landfill sites, because hot, dry conditions increase the risk.
"The fire at the Selalang Landfill in Sarikei affected an area of 1.5ha. As of today, about 1.3ha (87 per cent), has been extinguished, with firefighting efforts continuing on the remaining 0.2ha.
"Sarawak DOE will continue to monitor the fire site, including using drones to obtain the latest information on the fire's status and the extent of the affected area," she said.
She said air quality is also being monitored to assess the fire's potential impact on local air quality, with further action to be taken based on on-the-ground conditions and joint assessments with relevant agencies.
At the same time, Azuri Azizah said the DOE will continue monitoring API readings, hotspots, and developments in transboundary haze, using meteorological information to assess the situation and coordinate haze management efforts at district, state, and national levels.
She said coordinated measures are being implemented under the National Haze Action Plan, which provides, among other things, for the National Disaster Management Agency to activate the Disaster Management Committee if the API reading remains above 150 for more than 24 hours.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MCA ready for GE16 if polls called early, says Wee
Article:
BATU PAHAT: MCA is ready to face the 16th General Election (GE16) earlier than scheduled, party president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong said.
Wee said there was no guarantee the government would wait until the full five-year term was up before calling the election, based on the track record of previous general elections.
"I have already said in my speech that we actually need to shift into fifth gear now. We must always be prepared — not the kind of preparation where we only get ready today because we are going to contest tomorrow.
"MCA must ensure that election machinery and strategies are put in place early, including taking into account the different political conditions in each state," he said.
He said MCA's approach could not be standardised across all states, as Johor, Negri Sembilan and Melaka each had different political characteristics and varying levels of party strength.
"Each state has its own strategy. Johor is different from Negeri Sembilan, so we have to work harder in each state according to its own mould.
"We need to identify where our strengths lie, which areas we can win, and we must conduct a precise analysis," he said.
He was speaking after officiating the MCA Johor Annual Convention in Yong Peng here.
Wee, who is also the Ayer Hitam member of Parliament, said MCA had shown improvement following its performance in the recent Johor and Negeri Sembilan state elections.
"What is remarkable about MCA is that in Johor in 2018 we did not win a single seat, but in the 2022 state election we won four seats — all taken from DAP. This time we won another four, bringing the total to eight, and for the first time we surpassed the number of seats won by DAP. This is an achievement.
"But we must not get carried away with this success, because we still have a bigger mission. We need to consolidate more programmes to win the areas where we lost by a narrow margin. For example at the Stulang state seat, we lost by just over 600 votes," he said.
He said the same approach needed to be applied in Melaka and other states, with MCA identifying its strengths and potentially winnable seats based on precise analysis.
"If you have not started yet, find a place to start. We need to prepare early.
"We cannot be the kind of party that only gets ready today because we are contesting tomorrow. That is not the way," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KL attractions see many visitors going maskless amid haze on Malaysia Day
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Many people are still choosing not to wear face masks despite the haze, particularly at popular public attractions.
A check at the Sultan Abdul Samad Building and KLCC found many visitors going about their activities without masks.
Visitor Norherma Mokhtar, 35, said she opted not to wear one as she found it uncomfortable.
"Since the haze began, I have reduced my outdoor activities to avoid prolonged exposure.
"Today is a public holiday in conjunction with Malaysia Day, so I took the opportunity to visit the Sultan Abdul Samad Building with friends.
"We chose to spend time indoors rather than outside," she was quoted as saying.
She said she was also more cautious about spending too much time in crowded places.
Meanwhile, Sharifah Nadiah Syed Mohd Abd Rani, 35, said she visited the Sultan Abdul Samad Building at the invitation of friends after not having done outdoor activities for some time.
"I am aware of the risks of not wearing a mask in open areas. I have asthma and am grateful that I have not suffered an attack during this period.
"I always take precautions and make sure I drink enough water," she said.
Farhana Mat, 37, said she only wore a face mask when she expected to spend a long time outdoors.
"The air makes breathing uncomfortable. However, today I did not wear one as I was only stopping briefly at KLCC before entering Suria KLCC," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PH has yet to discuss Melaka polls with Rauf, says Amirudin
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: No discussions have been held with Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh on cooperation for the upcoming Melaka election, said Pakatan Harapan election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
Amirudin, who is also PKR vice-president and Selangor Menteri Besar, said he had yet to discuss the state election with Rauf.
He said the decision on when to dissolve the Melaka Legislative Assembly was up to the chief minister.
"You have to ask Rauf because he will decide when to dissolve the state assembly. After the dissolution, we will see whether there will be any negotiations," he told reporters after officiating the 2026 Islamic Book Festival at the Putra Mosque Auditorium here today.
Earlier, the Melaka
Chief Minister's Office denied a viral claim
that Melaka Yang di-Pertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Mohd Rustam and Rauf had signed a document to dissolve the state assembly today.
Head of Communications and Media at the Melaka Chief Minister's Office, Norhafizah Mohd Sati, said the office had not been informed of any meeting between the two leaders as claimed in the viral message.
Asked about Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's call for those who wanted Umno and Barisan Nasional removed from the unity government to do so formally, Amirudin said there was no need to prolong the matter for now.
"When the cabinet meets, raise it there if you want to remove BN from the unity government," he said.
He said the government was focused onresolving economic issues and matters concerning the people's interests.
On the "priest and nun joke" shared by Sepang Umno division chief and Dengkil state constituency coordinator Datuk Noorazli Said, Amirudin said the matter would be discussed at the Selangor executive council meeting if necessary.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Palestinians are the real victims, Thunberg tells Ed Sheeran
Article:
STOCKHOLM: Swedish activist Greta Thunberg and other activists have called out British superstar Ed Sheeran after rapper Macklemore was dropped from his tour for making pro-Palestinian comments while performing.
Sheeran has denied being behind the decision to remove Macklemore, saying his tour's promoter was responsible, but several supporting acts have announced they were quitting the tour.
"Ed, there is only one victim here: the Palestinian people," Thunberg, together with activist group Humanti Project, said in post to Instagram late on Tuesday.
According to a post by Sheeran, where he stressed the decision was the promoters, venues on the tour "communicated that they would pull the shows if he was still supporting."
Finneas – a performer also famous for work with his superstar sister Billie Eilish – Irish acts Aaron Rowe and Beoga, and Lukas Graham of Denmark have all posted they were quitting Sheeran's "Loop Tour."
"This is a clear and undeniable sign that the global consciousness has shifted. The normalisation of an apartheid state, and the attempts to sanitise or justify its actions, will no longer be tolerated," the post shared by Thunberg said.
While opening for Sheeran earlier this month at New Jersey's MetLife Stadium, Macklemore shouted "Free Palestine!" and told Palestinians they were "not forgotten."
In his post Tuesday, Sheeran touched on his decision not to comment publicly about political subjects, notably the war in Gaza.
"I am not complicit. I have my personal views on this devastating conflict. Just because I choose not to speak publicly, it doesn't mean I don't care," he said.
Macklemore, known for hits including "Thrift Shop" and "Can't Hold Us", has long vocally supported Palestinians.
In 2024 he released "Hind's Hall," which pays tribute to Hind Rajab, a five-year-old Palestinian girl whose death sparked a wave of international outrage.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fuel prices rise 35 sen amid Middle East tensions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The retail prices of RON97, unsubsidised RON95 and unsubsidised diesel will rise by 35 sen a litre for the Sept 17 to 23 period, according to the Finance Ministry.
Based on the Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM) formula, RON97 will rise from RM4.50 to RM4.85 a litre, while unsubsidised RON95 will increase from RM4.02 to RM4.37, the MOF said.
It said unsubsidised diesel will rise from RM4.92 to RM5.27 a litre.
Tensions in the Middle East had intensified following more than 200 days of conflict, it said.
"Iran had attacked 10 vessels near the Strait of Hormuz in response to US attacks on five Iranian tankers, while attacks had also spread to Yemen and Saudi Arabia's energy infrastructure.
"Vessel traffic through the Straits of Hormuz had fallen to single-digit levels following the escalation in attacks," MOF said in a statement today.
The situation worsened when drone attacks temporarily halted operations along Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline, one of the main routes bypassing the Straits of Hormuz.
Talks between Iran and Gulf countries on the security of shipping routes had also been postponed.
"These developments pushed Brent crude oil prices back above US$100 a barrel, reaching nearly US$110 a barrel during the APM calculation period," MOF said.
Meanwhile, refining margins remained high following disruptions to refining capacity in Russia, it said.
"Constraints on crude oil supplies and disruptions to refining capacity continue to limit refined petroleum product output, putting further pressure on global petroleum prices."
MOF said rising tensions in the Middle East and the Russia-Ukraine conflict could prolong volatility in petroleum prices.
"The Madani government will continue to protect the people and businesses from the impact of this global uncertainty, including by maintaining targeted Budi Madani subsidies for eligible users," it said.
Despite the increase in unsubsidised prices, eligible Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) recipients will continue to pay RM1.99 a litre for RON95.
This means the government will bear a subsidy of RM2.38 a litre, equivalent to 54 per cent of the unsubsidised price of RM4.37.
Eligible Budi Madani Diesel (Budi Diesel) recipients will continue to pay RM2.10 a litre for diesel, compared with the unsubsidised price of RM5.27.
The government subsidy amounts to RM3.17 a litre, or 60 per cent of the unsubsidised price.
The subsidised fuel prices remain as follows:
RON95 (Budi95)
: RM1.99 a litre
Diesel (Budi Diesel)
: RM2.10 a litre
Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS)
: RM2.05 a litre
Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS)
: RM2.15 a litre
Through Budi95 and Budi Diesel, eligible Malaysians can continue to purchase subsidised RON95 and diesel using their MyKad, subject to their monthly eligibility limits, MOF said.
It said the basic monthly eligibility limit for BUDI95 and BUDI Diesel had been increased to 300 litres from Sept 1.
Eligible owners of diesel-powered pickup trucks and jeeps will also receive an additional 100 litres, bringing their total monthly eligibility to up to 400 litres.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Keretapi Sarong: Media Prima truck draws visitors at TRX
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Media Prima Berhad's (MPB) "Wajah Malaysia" mobile truck drew visitors at the 2026 Keretapi Sarong event at The Exchange TRX here today with free personalised newspaper front-page prints and interactive activities.
MPB Group Marketing manager Hana Hatim said visitors to the Petronas-sponsored truck could have their photographs taken and receive a free personalised A3-sized newspaper front page.
"Throughout the day, our emcee will also conduct various games on stage, giving visitors who take up the challenges the opportunity to win exclusive 'Wajah Malaysia: Nadi Negara, Cerita Kita' prizes," she said when met at the event today.
Visitor Nur Irsya Humaira, 20, a student, said today was her first time attending Keretapi Sarong and described the experience as lively and meaningful.
She said she and her friends left their homes at about 8am and travelled from Putra Heights to Subang via the LRT before joining the gathering.
"It was very crowded but fun because everyone was so happy and dressed in traditional attire," she said.
Nur Irsya said the event also gave her a greater appreciation of Malaysia's diverse cultures, with Malaysians from different ethnic backgrounds embracing each other's traditional clothing and customs.
"As a young person, I was very excited to see everyone doing this. We come from different races and everyone was trying each other's cultures.
"I think this is very good for the younger generation because it shows that our cultures are beautiful and should be celebrated together," she said.
Hana said the truck's photo-printing service, which operates from 10am to 7pm, initially targeted 2,000 prints but the strong turnout could see the figure exceed 3,000.
She said visitors only needed to engage with the campaign's participating social media platforms to obtain their personalised newspaper front page, with designs from the New Straits Times, Berita Harian and Harian Metro.
"We started at 10am and will continue until 7pm. Visitors can continue enjoying the concert and other booths here," she said.
Hana said the event had attracted a larger crowd than initially anticipated, with visitors turning up in colourful traditional attire.
"The crowd has been very good. Even around our small truck, there has been a large crowd," she said.
The activation is part of MPB's "Wajah Malaysia" campaign, which the group designed to turn physical engagement at Keretapi Sarong into a wider national digital campaign involving an estimated 25,000 visitors.
Meanwhile, Media Prima will unveil its giant digital "Wajah Malaysia" mosaic today, featuring hundreds of portraits collected throughout the campaign.
Hana said the digital mosaic would be featured across Media Prima's platforms from midnight today until Sept 20.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Former Kosovo president Thaci sentenced to 25 years for war crimes
Article:
THE HAGUE: Former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci was found guilty of war crimes including murder, torture and illegal detention by the Kosovo war crimes tribunal on Wednesday.
Thaci, 58, was sentenced to 25 years in prison for crimes committed as top commander of the ethnic Albanian Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) during the territory's violent break from Serbia in the 1990s.
The tribunal said he was guilty of the murder of 96 political opponents and perceived collaborators with Serbian security forces by Kosovo Liberation Army forces during the conflict.
He was also convicted for the arbitrary illegal detention of 385 people, torture of 303 people and cruel treatment of around 50.
The court said Thaci had "actively participated in and encouraged crimes."
Thaci, who stood in silence as the judge read out the conviction and the sentence, had denied all charges.
The ruling was closely watched in Kosovo and Serbia, where the legacy of the 1998-99 conflict and Kosovo's 2008 declaration of independence remain a source of tension between ethnic Kosovo Albanians and Serbs.
Thaci remains a revered figure for many Kosovo Albanians, while the tribunal itself is deeply unpopular in Kosovo.
In Pristina, thousands of people watching the verdict on a big screen booed the verdict and chanted "Thaci, Thaci" as some burst into tears.
Outside the Kosovo Specialist Chambers in The Hague dozens of Thaci supporters had gathered ahead of the verdict waving KLA flags and chanting "UCK", the Albanian acronym for the army.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MMNOs face DNB accounting test in Q4
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's transition to a 5G dual network model is entering a critical phase, with mobile network operators (MNO) set to begin equity accounting for Digital Nasional Bhd's (DNB) financials in the fourth quarter (Q4) of financial year 2026 (FY26).
The move could provide greater clarity on the impact of DNB's financial and operational performance on the earnings and dividend outlook of its MNO shareholders, according to Kenanga Research.
CelcomDigi Bhd, Maxis Bhd and YTL Power International Bhd each hold a 33.3 per cent stake in DNB - and its equity accounting treatment is expected to materialise in Q4.
Kenanga Research said the developments of the dual network are largely reflected in CelcomDigi's current valuation as the stock is trading below its historical mean, and therefore offering greater downside protection.
"This, coupled with its more attractive risk-reward, makes CelcomDigi our preferred MNO play over Maxis.
"Under our bear and bull scenarios, CelcomDigi offers 37 per cent upside and 26 per cent downside, compared with 21 per cent upside and 20 per cent downside for Maxis,"  it said.
Kenanga Research said Maxis has less valuation cushion, as it already trades at historical mean. This reflects its stronger earnings delivery which helped support a reversal in consensus earnings downgrades since early-2025.
"Increasingly, we believe that earnings delivery, alongside 5G dual network developments, will be a key driver of MNO share price performance from hereon,"  it added.
Kenanga Research expects CelcomDigi's earnings to improve in the near term, as its targeted post-merger synergies are not fully reflected in either the firm's forecasts or consensus estimates.
"Faster-than-expected realisation of these savings could therefore catalyse a reversal in consensus earnings downgrades and support a recovery in valuation multiples.
"Consequently, CelcomDigi offers greater scope for positive earnings surprises relative to Maxis, in our view,"  it added.
Separately, Kenanga Research said it is less concerned about potential near-term DNB-related funding requirements, as its analysis suggests that both MNOs have ample balance-sheet capacity.
This enables them to absorb additional funding requirements in the near term without materially compromising their dividend capacity.
The bigger risk will be if shareholder funding becomes a long-term recurring commitment, persisting until DNB reaches sustainable cash-flow breakeven.
The firm kept its "Neutral"  call on the sector, with an "Outperform" call on CelcomDigi (target price: RM3.28) and "Market Perform" call on Maxis (target price: RM3.70).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia seals off 50 companies over forest and land fires
Article:
JAKARTA: Indonesia has sealed off 50 companies across eight provinces after forest and land fire hotspots were identified within their operational areas.
Deputy Environment Minister Diaz Hendropriyono said the move was part of law enforcement efforts, with authorities monitoring the firms to determine their involvement in the blazes.
"We are monitoring these companies and 50 have now been sealed off. This means there were fires there, and if it is proven that the companies were involved, sanctions will be imposed," he said, as reported by the Antara news agency today.
Meanwhile, the Forestry Ministry said 1,037 high-confidence hotspots were detected nationwide as of 9.05pm local time on Tuesday. This represents a drop of 400, or about 27.8 per cent, from 1,437 a day earlier, according to data from its SiPongi monitoring system.
Social media updates from the ministry showed that among the six priority provinces, Central Kalimantan recorded 266 hotspots, South Sumatra 245, South Kalimantan 72, Jambi 62, West Kalimantan 43, and Riau 15.
Hotspot numbers declined in Central, West, and South Kalimantan, while increases were recorded in South Sumatra, Jambi, and Riau, requiring continued intensive monitoring.
Joint teams are carrying out patrols, field inspections, and firefighting operations, supported by water bombing, aerial patrols, and weather modification operations where necessary.
Separately, Forestry Minister Raja Juli Antoni urged communities, farmers, and companies to remain vigilant against forest and land fires until late October or early November, warning that natural rainfall is expected to arrive later than previously forecast.
Citing updated forecasts from Indonesia's Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG), Raja Juli said rainfall previously expected in early October could be delayed until late October or early November.
"This means the very strong El Nino, similar to the one in 2015, will remain with us for about another one and a half months," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar says Tabung Haji asked to delay RCI report release
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) had asked the government to delay the release of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report after it was completed, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar said TH management made the request out of concern that releasing the report would trigger a mass withdrawal of deposits, potentially affecting its operations.
He said the matter was subsequently brought before the cabinet before a decision was made to delay the release of the report.
"TH asked us not to publicise it now (at that time).
"If we had publicised it then, there would have been no solution to the problem.
"People would withdraw their money and TH would be paralysed. That was proposed by the board.
"I asked TH chairman Tan Sri Rashid Hussain to come to the cabinet and explain the matter directly to the Cabinet ministers.
"So, the decision to release the RCI report was not mine, but the cabinet's.
"I proposed, but in the Cabinet, I asked each minister one by one. I asked the deputy prime minister and ministers what they thought.
"They agreed (to release the RCI report), and when I asked when, they said immediately. But on the condition that it could be debated in Parliament," he said when appearing as a guest on the Sembang OhhYeahh! podcast here today.
Anwar said when the RCI report was tabled in Parliament, Pas MPs walked out of the Dewan Rakyat and refused to listen to the debate.
"When it was brought to Parliament, Pas walked out. That is their problem, not mine... (they) asked what was the point of debating if Anwar was not there. At the time, I had undergone minor abdominal surgery.
"How many RCIs have been tabled before this? It is not the prime minister who has to table it. The relevant minister has to table it... then it can be debated.
"If I was well enough and came to Parliament afterwards, I would come and answer the questions (raised by MPs)," he said.
A special parliamentary sitting on the RCI report was held on Aug 11, during which Wawasan and Pas staged a walkout.
The walkout followed the rejection of the Opposition's request to postpone the special sitting due to Anwar's absence as he was recovering under medical supervision.
he RCI submitted its report in July 2022, and it was declassified on July 29 this year.
